title: Personal Credit Cards: Whether an Automatic Payment Instruction Reaches the Minimum Due
content:
A Personal Credit Cards account may carry an automatic payment instruction of one of several kinds. For the question whether a missed debit was the bank's failure, what matters is whether the instruction on the card, as it stands when the matter is handled, would have taken at least the minimum payment due on the card's most recent statement.

## Rule

| Instruction on the card | Reaches the minimum due |
|---|---|
| Minimum payment due | yes |
| Full statement balance | yes |
| Fixed sum no smaller than the minimum payment on that statement | yes |
| Fixed sum smaller than that statement's minimum payment | no |
| No automatic payment | never |

An instruction that reaches the minimum is one that, had the debit been taken on the due date, would have paid the statement's minimum in full.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

- The most recent statement's minimum payment due is 48.12 USD and the card carries a fixed instruction of 48.12 USD: the fixed amount equals the minimum, which counts as reaching it.
- The same statement with a fixed instruction of 48.11 USD: one cent short, so the instruction does not reach the minimum.
- A fixed instruction of 250.00 USD against the same minimum reaches it comfortably.
- A card whose instruction is set to take the statement balance reaches the minimum whatever the figures, as does one set to take the minimum payment due.
